nodes.title: Table G.1. Federal Reserve open market transactions, 2023 Millions of dollars
nodes.summary: The excerpt begins Appendix G, which contains 13 statistical tables on Federal Reserve operations. It presents Table G.1's detailed monthly and annual 2023 open market transaction data for Treasury, agency, and mortgage-backed securities, total holdings, and temporary repo and reverse-repo operations, together with methodological notes and source references. It then presents Table G.2's December 31 holdings of Treasury and federal agency securities for 2021–23, including maturity and security-type distributions and year-over-year changes, highlighting the substantial decline in Treasury holdings and the stable $2.347 billion level of agency holdings.

nodes.title: Table G.2. Federal Reserve Bank holdings of U.S. Treasury and federal agency securities, December 31, 2021–23 Millions of dollars
nodes.summary: The text presents Federal Reserve statistical tables covering 2021–23 holdings of Treasury securities, federal agency securities, mortgage-backed securities, and temporary repo transactions, with maturity, type, issuer, annual-change, valuation, collateral, and guarantee information. It also reports that reserve requirements for net transaction accounts, nonpersonal time deposits, and eurocurrency liabilities were all zero percent at year-end 2023, along with their effective dates and explanatory notes.

nodes.title: Table G.3. Reserve requirements of depository institutions, December 31, 2023
nodes.summary: The text presents reserve requirements and banking-structure statistics. Reserve requirements were 0 percent for net transaction accounts, nonpersonal time deposits, and Eurocurrency liabilities, with the stated effective dates and Regulation D reference. A second table compares 2022 and 2023 counts of banks, branches and additional offices, and bank-holding-company-affiliated banks, detailing new institutions, conversions, discontinued or ceased operations, other changes, and net changes, with breakdowns by bank type and explanatory definitions and coverage notes.

nodes.title: Table G.4. Banking offices and banks affiliated with bank holding companies in the United States, December 31, 2022 and 2023
nodes.summary: The excerpt contains two statistical tables. Table G.4 details changes in U.S. banks, banking offices, and bank-holding-company-affiliated banks between year-end 2022 and 2023, broken down by institutional type and including definitions and coverage notes. Table G.5A provides long-run and 2023 monthly data, in millions of dollars, on depository-institution reserves, Federal Reserve credit and its components, float, Treasury currency, special drawing rights, and gold holdings.

nodes.title: Table G.5A. Reserves of depository institutions, Federal Reserve Bank credit, and related items, year-end 1984–2023 and month-end 2023 Millions of dollars
nodes.summary: The text reproduces Federal Reserve statistical Tables G.5A and G.5B on reserves of depository institutions, Federal Reserve Bank credit, and related items, all in millions of dollars. Table G.5A covers annual year-end data from 1984–2023 plus monthly 2023 data, organizing figures into factors supplying reserve funds and factors absorbing them. It details Federal Reserve securities, repos, loans and emergency lending facilities, other assets, float, gold and Treasury-issued currency, alongside currency in circulation, Treasury accounts, reverse repos, term deposits, other liabilities, and reserve balances. Table G.5B provides the earlier year-end historical series for 1918–1983. The accompanying notes define the major components, explain changes in accounting treatment and the inclusion of special lending programs, identify discontinued or newly included categories, describe deferred assets and Treasury-related items, and caution that rounding may prevent components from summing exactly to totals.

nodes.title: Table G.5B. Reserves of depository institutions, Federal Reserve Bank credit, and related items, year-end 1918–1983 Millions of dollars
nodes.summary: The text reproduces Federal Reserve statistical tables. Table G.5B gives annual 1918–1983 data on sources and uses of reserve funds, Federal Reserve credit and assets, currency, gold, deposits, and member-bank required and excess reserves, together with extensive notes on definitions, historical changes, estimates, coverage, and rounding. Table G.6 compares the principal assets, liabilities, capital, and bank counts of U.S.-insured commercial banks by overall, national-member, state-member, and nonmember classifications for June 30, 2023 and 2022, with coverage and data-revision notes.

nodes.title: Table G.6. Principal assets and liabilities of insured commercial banks, by class of bank, June 30, 2023 and 2022 Millions of dollars, except as noted
nodes.summary: The excerpt contains two statistical tables from the 2023 Annual Report. Table G.6 presents June 30, 2023 and 2022 domestic assets, liabilities, equity, and bank counts for all U.S.-insured commercial banks, distinguishing total, member, national, state, and nonmember banks, with explanatory coverage, rounding, and revision notes. Table G.7 provides the historical percentage initial-margin schedule for short sales, margin stocks, and convertible bonds under Regulations T, U, and X from 1934 to 1974, followed by definitions, regulatory effective dates, the merger of Regulation G into U, and the historical customarily-required margin provision.

nodes.title: Table G.7. Initial margin requirements under Regulations T, U, and X
nodes.summary: The excerpt contains a historical table of initial margin requirements under Regulations T, U, and X for short sales, margin stocks, and convertible bonds, followed by explanatory notes on the regulations, effective dates, calculation of margin, and the former Regulation G. It then begins a detailed 2023-versus-2022 statement of condition for the Federal Reserve Banks, in millions of dollars, listing systemwide and individual-bank asset categories and values, including securities, loans, central-bank and settlement items, and other assets; total system assets and major securities holdings decreased in 2023.

nodes.title: Table G.8A. Statement of condition of the Federal Reserve Banks, by Bank, December 31, 2023 and 2022 Millions of dollars
nodes.summary: The text reproduces Federal Reserve statistical Tables G.8A and G.8B. Table G.8A gives 2023 and 2022 balance-sheet statements for the system and each of the 12 Reserve Banks, covering detailed assets, liabilities, capital, consolidated-entity interests, and explanatory notes. Table G.8B summarizes Federal Reserve note issuance and its collateral, including gold certificates, SDR certificates, and Treasury securities. All amounts are in millions of dollars, with rounding, valuation, consolidation, and notation conventions explained.

nodes.title: Table G.8B. Statement of condition of the Federal Reserve Banks, December 31, 2023 and 2022 Millions of dollars
nodes.summary: The excerpt contains two Federal Reserve statistical tables. Table G.8B compares the Reserve Banks’ note liabilities and collateral at year-end 2023 and 2022, showing outstanding notes, noncollateralized notes, collateralized notes, and matching collateral supplied by gold certificates, special drawing rights certificates, and Treasury securities, with a face-value/inflation-indexing note. Table G.9 presents 2023 income and expenses in thousands of dollars for the Federal Reserve System overall and the Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, and Richmond Banks. It details interest income by asset and activity, other income, total current income, extensive operating and interest expenses, net expenses, current net income, and gains or losses affecting current net income; the table continues beyond the supplied portion.

nodes.title: Table G.9. Income and expenses of the Federal Reserve Banks, by Bank, 2023 Thousands of dollars
nodes.summary: The excerpt presents Federal Reserve statistical tables on 2023 income, expenses, net income, comprehensive income, and distributions for the system total and all 12 Reserve Banks, detailing interest and other income sources, operating and financial expenses, gains and losses, Board assessments, variable-interest-entity results, and Treasury remittances. It also provides explanatory footnotes on accounting treatments, assessment allocations, rounding, and deferred remittances. A second table gives a long-run 1914–2023 series for all Reserve Banks, covering income, expenses, assessments, deductions, surplus and comprehensive-income transfers, dividends, statutory reserves, Federal Reserve note interest, and Treasury distributions, with unavailable historical categories marked n/a.

nodes.title: Table G.10. Income and expenses of the Federal Reserve Banks, 1914–2023 Thousands of dollars
nodes.summary: The text contains two Federal Reserve statistical tables. Table G.10 gives annual income, expense, assessment, transfer, dividend, Treasury-distribution, surplus, and comprehensive-income data for all Federal Reserve Banks from 1914–2023, followed by cumulative 1914–2023 totals for the system and each individual Reserve Bank, together with methodological and statutory footnotes. Table G.11 summarizes the principal departments' 2020–23 processing activity in millions of items and dollars, covering currency, coin, checks, securities, funds, and automated clearinghouse transactions, with notes on electronic checks, excluded reversals and non-value transfers, and revised figures.

nodes.title: Table G.11. Operations in principal departments of the Federal Reserve Banks, 2020–23
nodes.summary: The excerpt contains two statistical tables. Table G.11 presents 2020–23 Federal Reserve Bank processing volumes and dollar values for currency, coin, checks, securities, funds transfers, and ACH transactions, together with definitions and revision notes. Table G.12 presents December 31, 2023 counts and annual salaries for presidents, other officers, and full-time, part-time, and temporary/hourly employees across the Federal Reserve Banks and Federal Reserve Information Technology, including institution-level data, totals, and explanatory notes.

nodes.title: Table G.12. Number and annual salaries of officers and employees of the Federal Reserve Banks, December 31, 2023
nodes.summary: The text presents two Federal Reserve statistical tables for December 31, 2023. Table G.12 details presidents, other officers, and employees—including full-time, part-time, and temporary/hourly personnel—by Reserve Bank and Federal Reserve Information Technology, with counts, annual salaries, totals, and explanatory notes. Table G.13 gives property acquisition costs and net book values, including land, buildings, and other real estate, for all Reserve Bank offices and branches, with institution-level amounts, aggregate totals, and notes on construction-account allocation and the consolidation of Phoenix costs into Los Angeles.

nodes.title: Table G.13. Acquisition costs and net book value of the premises of the Federal Reserve Banks and Branches, December 31, 2023 Thousands of dollars
nodes.summary: Table G.13 reports, in thousands of dollars, the December 31, 2023 acquisition costs and net book values of premises for all Federal Reserve Banks and Branches. It provides location-level and aggregate amounts for land, buildings including vaults, total acquisition costs, and other real estate, including applicable n/a entries. Aggregate acquisition costs are $445.458 million for land, $3.488630 billion for buildings, and $3.934088 billion total, while other real estate totals $1.939828 billion. Footnotes address pending allocation of certain construction expenditures and the consolidation of Phoenix office costs into the Los Angeles Branch, followed by Federal Reserve publication and website information.

structure.summary: Appendix G compiles 13 statistical tables covering Federal Reserve operations, assets, liabilities, reserves, banking structure, regulation, finances, processing activity, personnel, and facilities. It presents current and historical data on open market transactions; Treasury, agency, and mortgage-backed securities; reserve requirements and reserve funds; insured commercial banks; margin regulations; Reserve Bank balance sheets, note collateral, income, expenses, distributions, and long-term financial results; operational processing volumes; employee numbers and salaries; and premises acquisition costs and book values. The tables include systemwide, Reserve Bank, bank-type, office-level, monthly, annual, and cumulative figures, supported by extensive notes on definitions, coverage, valuation, accounting changes, revisions, effective dates, rounding, collateral, and other methodological matters.
